items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: And the piano player I had in New York was named Frankie Frober.

ctx.x: George Potter. When I left New York, he stayed up there and he went with Tad Teeman. And the piano player I had in New York was named Frankie Frober. A lot of them called him Fraber. He made quite a reputation. They called him a backroom pianist. He used to wear a straw hat and all the daughters. Great piano player. But he was young and he was stricken with appendicitis and Harris Boyd. And so he wanted to stay up in the air. And he said, well, maybe he was greater in New York than he would have been in New York.…

No, no, no, no. I used to get the guitar. As the, well, according to some of the other interviews I've read, originally like some of the Dixieland bands here used the guitar a lot and then they found the- They used the banjo and then they switched the guitar. And then the banjo came in and then they went back to the guitar as time went on. What time did you incorporate a banjo or I mean a guitar, banjo then guitar in your larger orchestra? I used the guitar.
